messages.content: I want to finish the Minneapolis hotel. Put the two choices on the same basis, including every mandatory charge and breakfast if it is not included.

Aloft is $159 before taxes and its required facility fee; the one-night mandatory total is $184.76. Breakfast is not included, but you do not need to add it to the lodging total. The Transit Center Hotel is $151.42 including taxes, with no destination fee. Its breakfast is $18, making the comparable total $169.42 if you eat there.
When would each one charge me, and what are the actual cancellation deadlines?

Aloft takes a card guarantee now and charges at checkout. It can be canceled without penalty through 6:00 p.m. Central on Sunday, November 17; after that, the penalty is one night's room and tax. Transit Center charges the full $151.42 when booked. That advance-purchase rate is nonrefundable from the moment of booking.
How do they compare for Tuesday's roundtable, Wednesday's workshop, and getting to MSP afterward? Also confirm they will hold my bag Wednesday.

Aloft is beside the roundtable venue, about a three-minute walk, and roughly 12 minutes by hired ride to Wednesday's workshop. From the workshop, the planned rail trip to MSP is about 35 minutes. Transit Center is about 18 minutes from the roundtable by rail and walking, but it sits on the direct line to the workshop; that trip is about 14 minutes, followed by about 32 minutes to MSP. Both hotels confirmed complimentary bag storage after checkout for registered guests.
Does the cheaper one reduce transportation enough to matter, or does it just move the cost around?

It mostly moves the cost around. Transit Center would lower lodging by $33.34 if breakfast is skipped, but Tuesday's extra local travel brings the trip estimate to about $698.42. With breakfast, it is about $716.42. Aloft keeps the existing transportation estimate of $107, so airfare $418 plus hotel $184.76 plus transportation is $709.76.
Book Aloft. The refundable deadline and being next to Tuesday's venue are worth the small difference. Keep breakfast out, and leave the rest of the allowance as contingency.

Aloft Minneapolis is booked for one night, Tuesday, November 19, at a mandatory total of $184.76, payable at checkout. Cancellation is free through 6:00 p.m. Central on November 17, and post-checkout bag storage is confirmed. The trip estimate remains $709.76: $418 airfare, $184.76 lodging, and $107 transportation. That leaves $90.24 of the $800 allowance unassigned as contingency. Flight ticketing is still the remaining action.
